citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The Dallas World Aquarium does not currently have an attending veterinarian. On May 20, 2026, the attending vet
resigned from her position and is no longer consulting nor on call. The incoming attending veterinarian is potentially
scheduled to start July 20, 2026. Failure to have an attending veterinarian has contributed to numerous animals having
veterinary care issues at the facility. Each exhibitor shall employ an attending veterinarian under formal arrangements. An
attending veterinarian must be employed to ensure the animals are provided adequate veterinary care.
Correct immediately.

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
“Slim Jim” (ID 13A067), a female 13-year-old Little Penguin located in the facility veterinary clinic was observed unable to
stand or hold herself up. The inspector witnessed her dragging her front end and face along the soft sided enclosure. She
was repetitively trying to right herself without success. She was seen falling on her face and was unable to maintain an
upright posture. At one point “Slim Jim” flopped over and was unable to right herself. This behavior continued for the
approximate 30 minutes the inspector was in the room. “Slim Jim” was under medical care since April 21, 2026, for being
possibly egg bound and occasionally stumbling. On May 20, 2026, the Dallas World Aquarium attending veterinarian
resigned from her position. Since the AV’s departure the animal hasn’t been seen by a veterinarian and her condition has
rapidly declined.
Four Wattled Jacanas were acquired by the facility and brought to the clinic for treatment after arriving from shipment.
None of the Jacanas were evaluated by a licensed veterinarian. Two subsequently died of unknown causes on 25 May
2026 and 29 May 2026. The other two Jacanas reportedly suffered from broken and necrotic toes and are still at the
facility clinic under general staff observation. Failure to have sick or injured animals evaluated and treated by a licensed
veterinarian can result in serious harm or even death to the affected animals.
On 1 June 2026 a single young Oropendola was found outside of the nest, weak and in need of care. The animal was
taken to the facility clinic for treatment. This bird has not been seen by a licensed veterinarian. Radiographs taken by
facility staff showed what they believed was a broken toe. The animal is still present in the facility. Failure to have sick or
injured animals evaluated and treated by a licensed veterinarian can result in serious harm or even death to the affected
animals.
A crimson-rumped Toucan (ID# 21H061) has been under treatment for an eye problem at the facility clinic for multiple
weeks. A treatment sheet dated 30 May 2026 states that Lasix 10 mg/mL was prescribed for treatment by the owner of
the facility. The facility does not have an attending veterinarian at this time, and the owner is not a licensed veterinarian. A
non-veterinarian prescribing medical treatment for an animal is not an appropriate method of treatment and is a potential
source of harm to the animal being treated.
All birds must be seen by a licensed veterinarian by 12 PM on June 18, 2026.

2.75 (b)(1)
The provided acquisition records were inadequate and inanccurate for the 16 recently acquired Wattled Jacanas. An
invoice for 12 Wattled Jacanas was provided and the manager stated they weren’t charged for the 4 sick birds. Adequate
acquisition paperwork is important for disease tracking and accurate animal records.
Correct from this date forward.

Dead cockroaches were found in the fridge where freshly prepared animal feed is stored. Food shall be protected from
contamination. The fridge must be cleaned immediately.
Corrected at the time of inspection

The light fixture casing in the lockout area for the Giant River Otters has accumulated algae contaminated water. This is a
potential source of contamination of the enclosure. Fixture must be maintained in good repair.
Corrected at the time of inspection
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with an employee.
Additional Inspectors:
Michael Tygart, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
